Title

NS4R Software Developer

At KBR, we deliver science, technology and engineering solutions to governments and companies around the world. KBR employs approximately 37,000 people worldwide with customers in more than 85 countries and operations in over 28 countries. KBR is proud to work with its customers across the globe to provide technology, value-added services, and long-term operations and maintenance services to ensure consistent delivery with predictable results.

Trinzic is the future independent company to be created through the planned spin-off of KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business, expected in January 2027. Our people work at the frontier of what is possible, delivering solutions in challenging environments and advancing some of the world's highest-priority national security and space missions. 

Backed by decades of mission success, deep expertise, and trusted partnerships, Trinzic will launch as a global organization with more than 18,000 employees supporting customers around the world. Join us at a defining moment and help shape the future of a company built to tackle complex challenges and make a meaningful impact. 

Candidates who join KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business before the spin-off will transition to Trinzic when the separation is complete and will not need to reapply for employment. 

Job Summary

KBR is seeking an NS4R Software Developer to join our team in Colorado Springs, CO or El Segundo, CA.

This job supports SSC within the Joint Terminal Engineering Office (JTEO) as a developer on the National Security SATCOM Systems Synchronization Roadmap (NS4R) software application. The NS4R application is hosted on Defense Information Systems Agency’s (DISA) MilCloud and requires close coordination with DISA to resolve issues in a timely manner. In support of JTEO, duties include maintaining the NS4R database including security upgrades, development and implementation of enhancements to the NS4R tool, providing user held desk support, maintaining user accounts, providing NS4R database backups, maintaining configuration control and backups of the source code, support JTEO to evaluate and address security requirements and perform troubleshooting. The job requires the ability to assist Level 1 POCs with data entries and identify and correct incomplete or questionable data entries and management of the NS4R MilCloud Virtual Data Center (Memory/Storage/CPUs etc.). This also includes development and installation of patches to the Operating System and Data Base Server. As needed, you can expect to train Government and FFRDC personnel on the use and maintenance of the NS4R tool and database.

The MILSATCOM Systems Engineering, Integration, and Test (MSEIT) effort provides leading edge Systems Engineering & Integration (SE&I) for the Air Force’s Space and Missiles System Center. We support the Air Force’s acquisition of state-of-the-art Military Satellite Communications systems, providing global secure, survivable, and protected communications for our nation’s warfighters. We seek technical individuals who will thrive in a highly collaborative work environment of small teams, using the most modern tools and methodologies to tackle the challenges of integrating complex space and ground communications systems.

Required Experience

Active Secret clearance required for this position
Bachelor's degree in a STEM field
Experience working with military or DOW civilian clients and managing professional relationships
Strong interpersonal skills, communication (oral and written), and presentation skills
Capable in Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
2+ years of experience across the following software suites: Angular, Java, Microservices, Docker, DISA Stratus, VMWare

Preferred Experience

5+ years of experience across the following software suites: Angular, Java, Microservices, Docker, DISA Stratus, VMWare
2+ years of experience in SATCOM
INCOSE CSEP or ESEP certification

Work Environment

Location:
On-site

Travel Requirements:
Minimal

Working Hours:
Standard, 40 hours per week (Full-time)

Compensation

For Colorado Springs, CO only, the salary range for this position is approximately $94,000 - $117,400. For El Segundo, CA only, the salary range for this position is approximately $102,900-$128,600. The offered rate will be based on the selected candidate’s knowledge, skills, abilities and/or experience and in consideration of internal parity.

Other Compensation

KBR may offer bonuses, commissions, or other forms of compensation to certain job titles or levels, per internal policy or contractual designation. Additional compensation may be in the form of sign on bonus, relocation benefits, short term incentives, long term incentives, or discretionary payments for exceptional performance.

KBR Benefits

KBR offers a selection of competitive lifestyle benefits which could include 401K plan with company match, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, AD&D, flexible spending account, disability, paid time off, or flexible work schedule. We support career advancement through professional training and development.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you’re excited about making a significant impact in the field of space defense and working on projects that matter, we encourage you to apply and join our team at KBR. Let's shape the future together.

Overview

Job Description:

We don’t simply hire employees. We invest in them. When you work at Chatham, we empower you — offering professional development opportunities to help you grow in your career, no matter if you've been here for five months or 15 years. Chatham has worked hard to create a distinct work environment that values people, teamwork, integrity, and client service. You will have immediate opportunities to partner with talented subject matter experts, work on complex projects, and contribute to the value Chatham delivers every day.

Chatham Financials' Summer Internship Program offers a dynamic and immersive experience for aspiring technology professionals. This is your opportunity to gain hands-on software engineering experience in a leading finance and technology firm while contributing to projects that drive our business forward.

As a Software Engineering Intern at Chatham, you will be immersed in a collaborative team environment where you'll work alongside experienced engineers on cutting-edge products. Whether you're developing new features, optimizing systems, or solving complex problems, you'll play a key role in shaping the future of finance through technology.

Our technology team is made up of a team of Software Engineers, Testers, DevOps Engineers, Security Engineers, UX Designers, Quantitative Analysts and Data Base Analysts. We build software for our clients that range across multiple sectors and industries as well as tools for our internal users to help them better serve our clients. Our team is a global team located in four different countries and multiple time zones. We interact daily with each other as well as our key business stakeholders to ensure quality and speedy delivery of our product offerings.  

What You’ll Do

"Use AI workflows and AI coding assistants as peers and collaborators to help you deliver the best technology solutions for Chatham"
Assist with developing cutting-edge financial applications; develop innovative, high-quality, and robust web applications and micro services as part of our growing application development team. 
Be a member of an agile scrum team that owns development of a specific product or platform. 
Collaborate with other software engineering teams, design team, quant team, product owners and managers, and business stakeholders, while working on intern project. 
Develop software in our technology stack which is constantly evolving but currently includes .NET,  ASP.NET, React, Angular, TypeScript, SQL Server, RabbitMQ and Redis. 
Build automated unit, integration and front-end tests using xUnit, Moq, NSubstitute and Cypress among other technologies. 
Implement the build, test, deploy development cycle in CI/CD pipelines using Docker, YAML, Gitlab CI, and Hashicorp Nomad
Use AI workflows and AI coding assistants as peers and collaborators to help you deliver the best technology solutions for Chatham

What You’ll Need: 

Working towards Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. 
2 years of experience preferred
Experience with object-oriented languages such as C#, C++ or Java 
Experience with JavaScript and JavaScript frameworks (e.g. React) 
Experience with relational databases such as Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle or MySQL 
Understanding of Unit testing, Test-Driven Development and mocking frameworks 
Understanding of continuous delivery principles and processes 
Understanding of REST principles, Service-oriented architecture, and API development 
Understanding of continuous delivery principles and processes 
Proclivity towards refactoring and continuously improving OO code through agile development methods. 
Open-source development projects. 
Contributions to the local developer community. 
Quantitative and modeling skills with an ability to learn techniques in numerical optimization, data mining, simulation, or model calibration. 

This role offers flexibility and is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement.

Chatham Financial offers an entrepreneurial culture that rewards teamwork and innovation. We seek individuals who are natural leaders, quick learners, and fit our collaborative culture. Join us to develop your fullest potential, impact our clients and community, and kickstart your career in finance.

Apply now and become a part of Chatham Financial's legacy of excellence and innovation!

Applicants must be enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate academic program at the junior or senior level.

added.title: UI/UX Software Engineer - NREC
added.description:
At the National Robotics Engineering Center (NREC), it is our engineers and technicians who drive the breakthroughs that define our success. The members of our technical staff collaborate closely with leadership and multidisciplinary teams to design, build, and deploy sophisticated robotic solutions that address complex challenges in industrial, commercial and government sectors. Each project benefits from their expertise, creativity, and hands-on problem-solving, fueling progress and innovation across the organization.

As part of our dedicated team, you will work alongside world-class robotics professionals committed to pushing the boundaries of technology and redefining ideas into solutions for real-world applications. We foster a culture of professionalism, respect, and collaboration, offering a flexible and encouraging environment where you can sharpen your skills, lead impactful projects, and take control of your career development.

We are seeking a dynamic UI/UX Software Engineer for existing and new projects. In this position, you will work on a variety of user interfaces for robotic systems. You will have an opportunity to collaborate on an internal team and with sponsoring partners to support the work through all lifecycle stages. Our team has members with diverse backgrounds both in robotics and other industries aligned to make robust software and firmware that is useful in the world. Projects you may support range from industrial machine operator assist systems to agricultural productivity tools and beyond to other automation, autonomy, or safety systems. Your day-to-day work will include developing user interfaces for internal and external usage centered around robotic systems.

Your Primary Responsibilities Include

Co-Design Human-Machine Interfaces: Partner closely with robotics engineers, hardware teams, and field operators to design custom, intuitive interfaces for complex robotic systems.
Build Native Qt/QML Frontends: Develop fluid, hardware-accelerated user interfaces using QML and/or Qt, binding them smoothly to backend C++ or Python data streams.
Prototype & Test with Real Users: Prototype interaction flows and collaborate directly with end-users to evaluate usability, safety, and operator performance in the field.
Integrate Real-Time System Data: Connect UI components to central system state engines, telemetry feeds, and databases while ensuring the interface remains fast and responsive.
Champion Collaborative Software Development: Actively participate in an inclusive team culture through constructive peer reviews of both designs and code, integration testing, version control, and clear documentation.
Integrate & Adapt APIs: Adapt open-source libraries, proprietary tools, and backend APIs to extend UI capabilities cleanly and maintainably.
Cross-Functional Field Testing: Validate and refine interfaces through hands-on testing with both simulated environments and physical robotic hardware alongside the broader engineering team.

We're looking for an engineer to help manage how data is handled across Thinking Machines: what we collect and acquire, where it is stored, who and what systems can access it, how long we keep it, and how it's used in training, evaluation, and products. You'll help build the systems that let us protect privacy and make definitive statements about our practices from data inventory and classification through access and purpose controls to retention, deletion, and audit. You'll also collaborate closely with researchers and product engineers to answer privacy questions that don’t have textbook answers.

This is a role for someone who knows privacy deeply and treats it as an engineering problem rather than a checklist. The questions we face are rarely settled by policy alone: what it means to honor a deletion request against a trained model; how customers' fine-tuning data on Tinker should be isolated, never commingled, and only used for the customer; when to deidentify data (and how) vs. apply differential privacy to it. We want someone who can weigh privacy against model quality, research velocity, and product usefulness, pick a defensible answer, and then build it.

What You'll Do

Implement and enforce privacy and data governance across internal systems day to day by building systems like data classification tagging, retention jobs, deletion pipelines, and data classifiers and integrating them across systems at Thinking Machines.
Build the isolation guarantees that keep customer and user data separate and protected, including the training data customers bring to Tinker and the conversations people have with our interfaces.
Run privacy reviews and threat models on new data sources, training runs, and product features, and close them out by shipping the control, the check, or the tooling, not only a recommendation.
Translate legal and policy requirements (GDPR, CCPA, contractual commitments) into working code: policy-as-code, CI checks, and pipeline enforcement, built and maintained by you.
Maintain shared libraries and guardrails that make the private path the default, and fix them when they break or fall out of date.

Skills and Qualifications

Minimum qualifications
Built and shipped at least one production privacy or data governance system (retention/deletion pipeline, policy evaluation engine, data cataloging and/or lineage system, consent system, or similar) and owned it through to operation, not just design.
Written and operated production code in Python or a comparable language, evidenced by a system you can walk through in detail: what it does, how it fails, how you debugged it.
Direct experience with enforcing privacy or governing data in an AI/ML data pipeline (training data, fine-tuning, inference, or evaluation) and can describe a specific privacy risk you identified or mitigated in one of these systems.
Has chosen pragmatic controls over ideal ones on real systems, and can describe what was shipped as a result.
Has written a technical requirement or control directly from a legal or policy obligation (GDPR, CCPA, or similar), and can name the obligation and the control.

Preferred qualifications
Experience at an AI lab or with ML infrastructure: training data curation, multi-tenant fine-tuning platforms, or inference systems that handle user data.
Has implemented a privacy-enhancing technique (deidentification, differential privacy, secure enclaves) in a real system, and can describe where it fell short.
Experience building data lineage, metadata, or policy-engine tooling, or large-scale deletion and retention systems.
Background in security engineering, or has worked directly with a security team on access control implementation.
Has been one of the first engineers building out a privacy function, and can point to the specific systems they personally built, not just the program they ran.

Logistics

Location: This role is based in San Francisco, California.
Compensation: Depending on background, skills and experience, the expected annual salary range for this position is $300,000 - $350,000 USD.
Visa sponsorship: We sponsor visas. While we can't guarantee success for every candidate or role, if you're the right fit, we're committed to working through the visa process together.

added.title: Robotics Software Engineer, Autonomy
added.description:
Join Us, and Ship Robots

Weave was founded to build the robots we’d want to have in our own home. We believe the next generation of robotics will transform everyday life by enabling people to do more and to reclaim time to spend on what’s important.

We also believe robots are in a sense like any other product: to matter, they have to ship. Our robots are already operating in real homes and businesses, giving us the opportunity to rapidly improve from real-world experience. With a growing team, strong customer demand, and capital for expansion, we’re entering an exciting stage of growth—and we’re looking for people with exceptional talent and standards to help bring home robotics to millions of households.

The Role

Weave is building robots that work in real customer homes. We’re looking for a software engineer with strong robotics fundamentals who enjoys developing algorithms, designing systems, and making them work on physical machines. You’ll develop software for localization, motion planning, and autonomy, with a role in the architecture that connects these capabilities. The work spans mathematical modeling, algorithm development, sensor integration, and system validation. You should enjoy making thoughtful design decisions and following an idea from its formulation through implementation and measured performance on a robot.

We value strong fundamentals, practical judgment, and curiosity across disciplines. You might bring years of experience developing robotic systems, or a smaller set of substantial projects that demonstrate depth and resourcefulness. There’s room to investigate new methods and deepen your expertise, with success measured by what our robots can reliably do.

What You'll Do

Localization and state estimation: Develop algorithms that combine IMUs, cameras, wheel odometry, and other measurements to estimate robot motion and maintain reliable localization.
Trajectory analysis and motion planning: Analyze robot trajectories and develop planning algorithms that account for geometry, kinematics, obstacles, and execution constraints.
System architecture and validation: Make system-level decisions about computation, timing, data flow, and component responsibilities. Define metrics and validation methods to assess accuracy, latency, robustness, and overall behavior.
AI and autonomy: Assess research in AI and robotics, evaluate emerging autonomy architectures, and integrate promising approaches where they improve robot capabilities and reliability.
Sensors and hardware: Integrate and characterize sensors, manage calibration and synchronization, and understand how hardware limitations and environmental conditions affect algorithm performance.
Software architecture: Design maintainable C++ and Python software, clear interfaces, and reliable communication across the robotics stack, using ROS 2 and other frameworks or custom infrastructure as appropriate.

What You'll Bring

Hands-on robotics experience: You’ve implemented and tested algorithms on physical systems and worked through the gap between a clean formulation and imperfect hardware.
Strong mathematical foundations: You’re comfortable with linear algebra, coordinate transformations, probability, and numerical optimization. You can reason about uncertainty, assumptions, and failure modes.
Depth in a core robotics discipline: Substantial experience in state estimation, sensor fusion, SLAM, motion planning, trajectory optimization, or control, with an interest in learning adjacent areas.
Algorithmic understanding: You understand the principles behind the methods you use. Relevant experience might include Kalman or particle filtering, factor graphs, bundle adjustment, graph search, constrained optimization, or model predictive control.
Strong software engineering: Experience implementing algorithms in C++, using Python or similar tools for experimentation and analysis, and contributing to maintainable software within a team.
Experimental judgment: You can design an informative experiment, compare results against ground truth or other meaningful references, and distinguish an algorithmic limitation from an integration or sensor problem.
Curiosity and ownership: You’re willing to investigate unfamiliar parts of the system and carry a problem through to a tested solution.

Nice To Have

Experience integrating multiple sensor modalities, including cameras, IMUs, wheel encoders, LiDAR, or radar.
Experience with sensor characterization, calibration, system identification, or parameter estimation.
Experience deploying algorithms under onboard compute, power, or latency constraints.
Familiarity with ROS or ROS 2.
Experience with mobile robots or mobile manipulators.
Experience evaluating learned methods for perception, estimation, or planning.

You don’t need experience in every area listed. We’re interested in the systems you’ve built, the fundamentals you understand deeply, and how you approach problems you haven’t solved before.
